newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RAND, DISEASE MAY PROMPT MORE SAFRICA MAIZE EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: RAND, DISEASE MAY PROMPT MORE SAFRICA MAIZE EXPORTS.

text.p: Continued weakness in the rand may lead to more exports of South African yellow maize as prices became more attractive, shrinking the surplus anticipated for this season and shoring up the recent price slide.

Market sources said on Friday there was continual demand for the grain from the East and the Pacific Rim, where the El Nino weather phenomenon has spawned a dry spell which may force countries there to up their import requirements.

"There has been a bit of a stand-off between our farmers who are not prepared to meet the prices they are being offered and buyers who don't seem to be prepared to pay the premium for our quality of maize," said an international commodity trader.
"However, as the rand depreciates and the overseas corn market remains fairly firm, our price ideas get closer and closer.
"I would imagine that if we see a little bit more weakness in this rand we will possibly be getting very close to levels where we can trade into the Pacific Rim and Japan," he added.

The rand, tracking a rampant dollar, on Thursday fell to its lowest level in seven months when it breached 4.70 -- bringing its losses in the past two weeks to over 15 cents. On Friday it came off its lows to trade at 4.67.
"The more our prices come into line with the price ideas of the buyers, we will be able to export more and we are going to have a tight scenario on yellow maize again," another trader said.
Chicago corn prices have in the past month recovered from two year lows despite expected record harvests.

Concerns about the early and intense build-up of El Nino, which has in the past wreaked havoc with weather conditions and ravaged agricultural output, would add further support to yellow, as well as white, prices especially in later months.
Yellow maize futures have this week risen off lows, with the September contract adding four rand on Thursday to 541 rand, December putting on five rand to 585 and March, 1998 rising one to 620.

The National Maize Producers Organisation said that white maize may start being channelled to Zambia as that country's import needs rose following worse-than-expected crop damage from grey leaf spot disease.
"That means the Zambian import requirement may have to rise dramatically. We have indications that Zimbabwe won't be able to fill this requirement," Giel van Zyl, Nampo's general manager said.
"So some more white maize will move there from South Africa."
South Africa has already exported sizeable quantities to Kenya following a drought there, keeping white prices firm amid concerns of a local shortage.
